Visuals.all: The city holds together and reads clearly. Building textures are plausible, and the frames show warm low-sun lighting, real-time shadows, haze and bikes, railings and market stalls as props. Geometry is still blocky, though: shopfronts are flat boxes, goods and stalls are cube-like, and facades are repetitive with little wear or clutter. Characters are small and low-detail, the combat frames show flat primitive props, and pale billboard-like stand-in objects appear in the fights, so the result sits well below commercial quality.

Animation.all: Across all four walking frames the player stands in almost the same upright pose. I can't see any clear stride, arm swing or robe motion, so this looks like a minimal walk cycle at best. In the combat frames, attacks show up mostly as effects such as beams, rings, bursts and orbs, and the body doesn't visibly move to match them. The enemies are simple grey shapes that don't appear to animate, and I see no hit reactions, death animations, crowds or moving foliage, even though floating text like 'Staggered' suggests those systems exist.

Combat feel.hexweaver: Combat clearly works and has real feedback: crit and damage numbers, chain counters, Interrupted/Staggered/Vanquished callouts, ground sigils and spell trails, six spells including a shade_step dash, a boss with a three-phase bar and a 'Phase II' banner, and loot cards plus beams with rarity colours. The biggest gap is that the fight has no tension or readability: the boss dies at 11 s, the player takes only 38 damage and never drops below full HP, three frames in a row show no enemies, enemies are small and cluttered, and the camera gets blocked (frame 12 is against a wall, frame 3 is filled by a close enemy). Hit-stop, knockback and enemy telegraphs can't be seen, only one class was recorded so class differences can't be judged, and 3,828 sound voices in 60 s suggests audio spam.
Combat feel.pyromancer: The pyromancer uses six distinct spells, and the frames show readable hit feedback: damage numbers, chain counters, 'Staggered'/'Interrupted'/'Vanquished' callouts, red ground telegraphs and a three-phase named boss with a health bar. Loot shows rarity-coloured beams and pickup cards. But only one class is shown, and the VFX are often muddy, with full-screen orange and green washes and camera clipping into geometry (frames 2 and 4) that hurt readability. Nothing shows hit-stop or strong impact weight, and the enemy models are simple.
Combat feel.stormcaller: The fight shows the 60-anchor features working. There is a phased boss with a health bar, a Phase II banner, an enraged state and a Vanquished moment. Damage numbers include crits, and stagger labels, chain counters, rarity-tagged loot popups, six distinct spells and level-ups all appear on screen, alongside a high sound-voice count. The biggest gaps are readability and pacing. Spell VFX are muddy, with a white-washed blob at the boss kill and overlapping text clutter. No enemy attack telegraphs are visible. Enemies look like simple placeholder shapes, and about half the clip is empty traversal with no enemies, so the frames show little crowd control, hit-stop or formation play.
Combat feel.warden: The frames show the core feedback loop: floating damage numbers including crits, 'Staggered' labels, a chain counter, a boss with a health bar and phases (Phase II/III), earth spike and AoE ground effects, and loot popups colour-coded by rarity. Readability is often poor, though. A large opaque pale-blue sphere covers the player in many frames, and the screen gets cluttered with labels. Threat is low: the player took 0 damage across 60 s, about half the clip has no enemies, and pebble_shot makes up 54 of 76 casts, so combat looks repetitive. There is no visible hit-stop, knockback or enemy telegraphing.

Story presentation.all: The prologue has strong framing: a title card, letterboxed over-the-shoulder shots of named NPCs with portraits and role tags, dialogue choices with three replies, a quest tracker showing distance, a reveal of the Bellwarden boss and a quest-complete card with rewards. The writing is witty, the tone is consistent and the premise is clear, with Cambridge's Market Hill as the setting. Holding it back: the characters are simple low-poly figures with no visible expressions or animation, there is no sign of voice acting, the boss reveal is a static shot under a text box, and the dialogue choices look shallow.

UI polish.all: The class selection screen, dialogue panel and Satchel inventory share a consistent serif-and-gold theme. The inventory has clear slots, rarity-tagged tooltips and a stats footer. The combat HUD has health and mana bars, numbered cooldowns, a minimap and a boss bar. The biggest gap is that the talent screen (frame 4) shows no talent UI at all, so that system has no visible evidence. Combat frames also get cluttered: in the warden frame a loot popup overlaps the damage numbers and pickup text, and in the stormcaller frame a quest-complete banner stacks on top of the combat effects, which hurts readability.
